purpose: Research baseline, not a parity or release certification

evidenceKinds.SEM: Positive and negative source/type/evaluator cases against pinned documented semantics and independent expected values.
evidenceKinds.ZK: Native lowering plus official checker/prover/verifier, including adversarial witness/public-input cases.
evidenceKinds.LEDGER: Isolated ledger finalized acceptance/rejection, exact state/events, atomicity and transaction binding.
evidenceKinds.ABI: Canonical byte/value representation, bounds, argument/result schema and artifact metadata fixtures.
evidenceKinds.HOST: Same portable artifact and vectors in at least two independent host-language runners.
evidenceKinds.PROVENANCE: Pinned source/tool versions, hashes, build/dependency closure and reproducible artifact manifest.

features.notes: Pinned compiler uses inclusive maxima internally. For ordinary Uint<0..m> and Uint<0..n>, addition returns exclusive bound m+n-1 and multiplication returns (m-1)*(n-1)+1. This contradicts the looser reference prose. Subtraction retains the left maximum and asserts a nonnegative result. Follow pinned implementation parity, not prose equations. Nominal aliases have separate checked-result rules.

sourceDerivedRules.appliesTo: Ordinary Uint operands and structural aliases, excluding nominal numeric aliases
sourceDerivedRules.maximumGuard: result inclusive maximum <= 2^248 - 1, checked before nominal result downcast
sourceDerivedRules.literalTyping: Literal v has minimal prefix range [0,v], not a singleton-refined type
sourceDerivedRules.declaredBinding: Declared const/parameter type controls later variable-reference inference
sourceDerivedRules.condense: Unwraps structural aliases and records nominal identities without shifting bounds
sourceDerivedRules.constantOptimization: Parameter cases do not depend on folding. expand-const splits declarations, and arithmetic inference precedes circuit simplification
sourceDerivedRules.nominalAliases: Same nominal identity and underlying type required. Result keeps original nominal type, with checked downcast when maximum grows

features.notes: Readable witness circuits and Helpers.Statement.forRange support half-open Native ranges with literal bounds, at most 1024 iterations and a preflight nested expansion budget. Body types are checked even when empty. Loop returns reject. Generic Helpers ranges accept compile-time Nat expressions through the same bounds and normalization after specialization. Readable container loops share the checked iteration backend. Native Rust, browser WASM and the pinned Compact oracle agree on the selected byte iteration and invalid callback. The guarded range finalized on Ledger 9 with exact state and private writes committed after finality. The Noctium range count cap is lower than the Compact limit. See tests/ReadableContainerLoop.lean and docs/development/structured-cells.md#finite-range-loops.

Staged Lean Iteration.applyWithLimits/mapWithLimits/foldWithLimits construct checked ordinary Helpers programs. Named helpers and anonymous statement bodies support inferred signatures and typed lexical captures. Fixed sequence map and fold accept vectors, structurally compatible tuples and scalar/composite byte sequences with equal lengths and checked scalar, Unit, record, tuple, nested-vector, byte and enum results with guarded tag/payload projections and canonical padding. Fold evaluates initial before sequence and requires exact accumulator/result types. Empty tuple callbacks accept omitted parameter types in typed return, binding and helper-argument positions. Arithmetic and Boolean operations require known operands. An unresolved map result uses the staged expectedElement type context. The hosted empty-tuple fixture with omitted annotations matches Compact 0.36.1 provider order, zero operator calls, result and state. Readable witness circuits support expression-bodied map/fold with inferred callback parameter types. The nested Bytes map/fold fixture matches Compact 0.36.1 provider order, return, and ledger total. Readable empty tuple callbacks support independently typed Bool and UInt uses. Native Rust and browser WASM run the same empty control plan. The Compact 0.36.1 oracle matches the provider order, zero operator callbacks and seed result. Statement-bodied syntax and automatic enclosing result types remain open. See docs/development/iteration.md, tests/EmptyTupleIteration.lean and tests/IterationWitness.lean. Unit arguments/captures and root Unit inputs retain logical arity with zero native fields, including generic specialization.

Compact permits sealing any ledger field and restricts writes by exported circuits. Noctium requires constructor initialization for sealed scalar and OpaqueString cells, rejects entrypoint and helper-body writes in source validation, and rejects prepared calls that change sealed state natively. Other sealed ledger types and Compact constructor/helper initialization semantics remain unsupported or unverified.

Depth-two ordinary and historic Merkle values under Bytes32 and Field map keys match Compact for setup, writes, reads and resets. Independent owner and bucket paths retain their exact state. Other nested value and path combinations require separate evidence.

Native primitive and claim proved. No inference of equivalence to generic transientHash, Merkle leaf hashing or Compact serialization.
Tagged UInt128 starting-balance read for either token namespace. A missing token reads zero.
Tagged strict greater-than predicate. Active comparisons follow the pinned VM's UInt64 operand boundary.
Tagged strict less-than predicate. Active comparisons follow the pinned VM's UInt64 operand boundary.

Strict UInt64 Unix-second comparison through the native ledger context. Focused checks cover equal and unequal cutoffs, guard outcomes, replay across a changed result and explicit disclosure. The native Rust client passes a checked prospective block context. Hosted client and composition qualification remain separate.

Strict UInt64 Unix-second comparison through the native ledger context. Focused checks cover equal and unequal cutoffs, guard outcomes, replay across a changed result and explicit disclosure. The native Rust client passes a checked prospective block context. Hosted client and composition qualification remain separate.

Typed optional caller from the ledger context, with absent, contract and user cases and both guard outcomes. The Rust SDK ordinary call covers a top-level absent caller. User inference during unshielded funding and live composed caller qualification remain open.

Guarded checkpoint emits a native marker between ledger writes. The scalar fixture matches Compact on marker presence and proves the ordered transcript. The native Rust SDK checks an actual finalized Ledger 9 prefix-only result for one timed call and keeps the private write staged through recovery.

Direct call-claim tests cover public target, entrypoint hash and control, require explicit commitment disclosure, and reject private target/hash/control or an undisclosed commitment. Named-interface composition covers one stateful route and aggregate call accepted on localnet. Other claim shapes and full Compact equivalence remain unverified.
Guarded native spend authorization by tagged token and contract or user recipient. Both recipient variants use independent keys.

Finalized native mint-funded receive, wallet-funded receive and partial-spend change each claim one guaranteed contract-owned output. Other offer shapes and a standalone public claim primitive remain open.
Whole and partial root Map spends finalize on Ledger 9.1.0.1 with ZKIR 3.2.1. The partial case claims one user output and one contract-owned change output for one qualified input.
The whole-coin Map spend claims the input nullifier derived for the contract-owned coin and finalizes on Ledger 9.1.0.1 with ZKIR 3.2.1. The native harness rejects replay.
Guarded native input accumulation by tagged token. Single UInt128 values and existing-key UInt64 addition follow the pinned VM.
Guarded native output accumulation by tagged token. Single UInt128 values and existing-key UInt64 addition follow the pinned VM.
Guarded native shielded mint by Bytes32 domain, with UInt64 amounts and accumulation. Transfer and settlement require separate ledger effects.

Guarded native unshielded mint by Bytes32 domain, with UInt64 amounts and accumulation. Recipient mint settlement is covered compositionally by deriving the contract color, recording a tagged spend claim, and adding a self-credit input only when a contract recipient matches the executing contract.

Lean readSelf binds the executing contract address as Bytes32 in a native call. The checked fixture covers two addresses, active and inactive guards, caller/address distinction, and exact public storage and return.
Native/Bool subset only. Compact ADT value layout and method equivalence unverified.

structuredCellUpdate.scope: Typed Native/Bool/UInt cell statements inside structured helper bodies lower to ordered guarded native effects. Owning contract schemas constrain state identity, type and sealed status. The focused source/native case uses a Native cell, a disclosed private Bool guard, strict unused narrowing, read-after-write and a proof-bound return.
structuredCellUpdate.limits: Native checker and exact local state only. No new keys, proofs or deployments. Provider/private-state scheduling in the same body, maps/aggregates, finite loops and full structured proof/ledger qualification remain open. The optional historical Witness.Semantics model still has unmatched older Boolean/byte/curve families and does not qualify this extension.

features.notes: Typed Lean scalar reset lowers to the existing cell write. Focused Compact 0.36.1 and ZKIR 3.2.1 native cases use the same seeded Native/Field, UInt64, Bool and Bytes4 cells, checking both guard outcomes and reads after reset. Aggregate cells and other type combinations remain unqualified.

features.notes: A direct Lean effect qualifies an already-booked self-contract coin into a root composite Cell. The native test stores the exact record at allocated index 42 and rejects absent or wrong-recipient bookings. It uses the pinned Cell fragment without recording a receive claim. Other recipients and live ledger qualification remain open.

Standalone and nested Bytes8 Counters accept checked UInt16 expressions or existing u32 literals. The selected Compact and Noctium cases agree on a runtime decrement and underflow rejection. Noctium binds one Subi immediate per update. Full host and deployment equivalence remain unverified.

Standalone and nested Bytes8 Counters accept checked UInt16 expressions or existing u32 literals. The selected Compact and Noctium cases agree on zero, three and maximum UInt16 amounts, out-of-range input rejection, and inactive missing paths. Noctium binds one Addi immediate per update. Full host and deployment equivalence remain unverified.

Native strict comparison with a UInt64 expression works on standalone and nested Bytes8 Counters. Reads observe earlier updates. Equality and inactive reads bind false. Active missing or malformed values reject.
Reads the UInt64 value of a standalone or nested Bytes8 Counter, including earlier updates in the same entrypoint. An inactive read binds zero. The host ledger getter remains unqualified.
Reset writes the Bytes8 UInt64 zero value to a standalone Counter or a nested leaf. It also initializes an absent leaf under existing parents. Inactive reset skips mutation.

Ordered insertion into standalone or map-nested Sets. The matched Native-parent and Bytes32-member case covers duplicate insertion and a finalized localnet insertion. A separate native fixture covers Curve25519Point members. Qualified shielded-coin insertion uses a separate method.

A root Set accepts an exact QualifiedInfo record with a coin index booked for the current contract. The native query-context fixture preserves existing members, checks idempotent insertion, and rejects missing or wrong-recipient bookings. Finalized ledger execution and broader recipient cases remain open.

Binds native Boolean emptiness for a standalone or map-nested Set. The matched case uses Bytes32 members and a Native parent. An inactive read binds false and skips path access. The host ledger method remains unqualified.

Reads ordered member presence from standalone and nested Sets. The matched case uses Bytes32 members and Native parent keys. The native foreign-key case also covers Curve25519Point members. The host ledger method remains unqualified.

Removes Bytes32 members in the matched standalone and nested case. An absent member leaves the Set unchanged. A separate native fixture exercises removal of Curve25519Point members. General composite member keys remain open.
Clears an ordinary standalone or nested Set. The matched Bytes32 member case preserves sibling Sets. The Curve25519Point fixture also initializes a missing Set under an existing map.
Binds the UInt64 count of distinct members after mutation. The matched case covers standalone and nested Sets with Bytes32 members and a Native parent key. The host ledger method remains unqualified.

The native snapshot ABI pages top-level Set members through declared scalar codecs and stable key order. The pinned Compact fixture compares exact member contents in both insertion orders. Nested Sets and SDK adapter qualification remain open.

Source upserts ordered scalar entries and writes checked records. Native examples cover Bytes32 keys, structured Native updates, qualified foreign keys, and mixed Native, Bytes32 and JubjubPoint records on direct and nested paths. Generic ADT values and all Compact overloads remain open.

structuredMapUpdate.scope: Typed map lookup, membership and upsert statements inside structured helper bodies reuse ordered native effects and closed lexical key/value expressions. Source/native evidence uses Bytes32 keys, Native values, nested guards, missing-entry insertion, existing-entry update and post-write returns.
structuredMapUpdate.limits: Current 3.2.1 native checker and local state only. No new keys, proofs, deployment or historical compatibility campaign. Values are Native/Bool/UInt; the native case exercises Native. Nested ledger trees, aggregate values, integrated provider/private-state scheduling and generic preservation remain open.

features.notes: Mint-funded receive, wallet-funded receive and partial-spend change finalize on Ledger 9.1.0.1 and store the assigned index in a root Bytes32-keyed Map. General Map.insertCoin remains open.

insertDefault writes the admitted typed default to a direct or nested Map entry. A pinned Field fixture compares insertion, replacement, membership and size. The native case exercises nested scalar, checked record and collection layouts. The nested HistoricMerkle case matches Compact on empty history after default insertion or replacement, history after append, and root-zero membership after explicit reset. Full type, proof and ledger qualification remain open.

Binds native Boolean emptiness for a direct or nested Map path. The matched Set fixture also checks the empty and populated outer Native-keyed Map. Inactive queries bind false without accessing the path. The host ledger method remains unqualified.

Reads ordered scalar or checked record values from an existing direct or nested Map key. Native evidence includes Bytes32 keys, guarded Native reads, and mixed Native, Bytes32 and JubjubPoint records. An active missing read rejects. Callers use membership and guards for defaults. ADT-valued lookup results and the host ledger method remain open.

features.notes: Binds Boolean presence on direct and nested Map paths and observes earlier writes. Native cases cover Bytes32 and qualified foreign keys and a guarded structured Native upsert. Inactive queries bind false. The host ledger method remains unqualified.

features.notes: Removes a leaf on a typed direct or nested Map path. An absent final key leaves the map unchanged, an absent parent rejects, and a false guard skips access. Native evidence covers nested Bytes32-keyed records and direct or nested foreign-keyed scalar maps.

Reset lowers to native empty-map replacement for a standalone or nested Map. A matched in-memory Compact 0.36.1 and Noctium case clears a two-entry Map, returns size zero and absent membership, and checks the exact empty native Map after-state. Full equivalence remains unverified.

The source size statement and native Map or Set size operation bind UInt64. Inactive queries bind zero. The existing checker fixture exercises the shared operation on Sets. Dedicated Map size comparison and host qualification remain open.

The native snapshot ABI pages top-level Map entries with scalar keys and values in stable key order. The pinned Compact fixture compares exact contents in both insertion orders. Nested Maps, compound values and SDK adapter qualification remain open.

Scalar and named-record Lists expose strict head and headOrDefault. Strict head requires a nonempty List. The optional form binds presence and a typed scalar or the declared record fields. The matched Native and Bytes128 case checks empty and nonempty values. The matched UInt8 case returns a single typed Maybe view on both compilers, with tag first and canonical zero for an empty List. The host ledger getter remains unqualified.

List isEmpty binds a Bool from the ordered native length read. The matched fixture covers standalone Native and nested Bytes128 Lists. A false guard skips the path and binds false, including an absent nested path. The host method remains unqualified.

Reads UInt64 length from scalar and checked named-record Lists, including nested paths. The matched fixture checks lengths after prepend, pop and reset. A guarded inactive read binds zero. The host length method remains unqualified.

Removes a nonempty head from a standalone or nested scalar or named-record List. The matched Native and Bytes128 case checks the next value and length. Noctium checks and rejects an empty pop in the VM. Matched Compact empty-pop behavior remains open.

Prepends a scalar or named record to a standalone or nested List. Public writes require explicit disclosure of private values and activity. The scalar fixture covers Native, Bytes0 and Bytes128, including a present zero-byte element. Named-record evidence covers Native, Bytes32 and JubjubPoint fields. General aggregate and coin element shapes remain open.
Qualified shielded-coin insertion requires a coin index allocated in the current transaction. The coin-valued method remains open.

Reset writes the empty native List sentinel and initializes an absent List leaf under an existing parent. The matched scalar case checks standalone and nested resets and their typed defaults. The Native-record fixture preserves sibling paths.

The native snapshot ABI validates the linked FAB shape and pages top-level scalar Lists in head-to-tail order. The pinned Compact fixture matches empty and nonempty views. Nested Lists, compound elements and SDK adapter qualification remain open.

Ordinary root-only checks compare a Field against the current Merkle root. The guarded read returns false when skipped. Depth-two native results match Compact for empty, populated and same-call append cases. The nested ledger ADT row covers the depth-two typed path fixtures.

Native, Bool, bounded UInt, fixed Bytes, and checked flat named records lower through the mdn:lh digest. Pinned Bool, mixed record and JubjubPoint cases compare roots and cursor. Under ZKIR 3.2.1, all nine standalone foreign Base, Scalar and Point append cases match pinned Compact leaf digests and roots. Nested composite leaves need separate evidence.
Root-only Bytes32 digest append. Depth-two roots and cursors match the pinned Compact fixture. The nested ledger ADT row covers prehashed append at a typed path.

Ordinary root writes accept a prehashed Bytes32 leaf and a disclosed UInt64 index. Depth-two native roots and cursors match Compact for sparse writes and replacement. The active operation rejects an out-of-range index.

Typed scalar and flat record writes bind the declared leaf encoding and a UInt64 index. Pinned Field, Bool and mixed record cases cover sparse insertion and active out-of-range rejection. Pinned JubjubPoint identity writes also match the native digest and root.

Indexed writes hash the declared scalar or record default. The pinned Bool and mixed record cases replace index zero while preserving the cursor at capacity. Pinned JubjubPoint identity writes also match the native digest and root.
Root-only fullness reads match the pinned Compact fixture before and after append. The native checker rejects an altered capacity result.
Root-only reset restores the exact initial native state. The depth-two fixture also compares the empty root and cursor with Compact.

Rust and C++ find the first stored match and return no path for missing leaves. Pinned Compact fixtures cover Field, Jubjub, all nine foreign curve roles, and structured and aligned FAB leaves. Search handles shared and collapsed tree nodes without expanding repeated branches.
Rust and C++ return the append cursor as canonical decimal across root and nested snapshots. Pinned Compact cases cover an empty tree and a sparse write in a two-key map.

Rust and C++ match Compact candidate roots and siblings for matching and substituted leaves. Indexed reads accept materialized sparse branches, including at the append cursor, and reject missing or out-of-capacity branches.
Rust and C++ return the same root for named root and nested trees. The pinned Compact oracle qualifies insertion roots for checked Field, curve, structured and aligned FAB leaves.
Root-level membership sees roots retained by earlier writes, including writes in the same call. Private expected roots require disclosure.
Typed scalars and flat named records lower through the mdn:lh leaf digest. Pinned Field, Bool and mixed record cases compare the root, cursor and retained history.
Root-level Bytes32 digest appends retain both previous roots and the updated root.
Root-level prehashed indexed writes preserve the highest append cursor, record the new root and reject out-of-range indices.
Typed scalar and flat record writes support sparse indices and replacement at capacity. Pinned Bool and mixed record cases compare roots, cursor and retained history.
Indexed writes hash the declared scalar or record default and retain the resulting root. Pinned Field, Bool and mixed record cases compare replacement after sparse writes.
Root-level fullness follows the append cursor, including after sparse writes and replacement at capacity.
Root-level resetHistory keeps the current root and append cursor. The guarded read observes the reset when active.
Root-level full reset restores an empty tree, cursor zero and the initial root in history.
Rust and C++ reproduce stored-leaf paths for historic trees across the pinned curve and structured corpus. Missing leaves return no path.
Rust and C++ report the historic append cursor, including the full-capacity sentinel after a sparse indexed write. The values match the pinned Compact snapshot.
Rust and C++ page historic digests from the same tagged state. The collected digest set and root agree with the pinned Compact snapshot.
Rust and C++ return candidate roots separately from the snapshot root, with sibling order matching pinned Compact. Checked lookup requires a stored match.
Rust and C++ return the current historic digest from root and nested snapshots. The pinned Compact oracle agrees on append and sparse indexed states.

Scalar native List heads return the typed Maybe shape. Matched Compact 0.36.1 and Noctium on ZKIR 3.2.1 UInt8 cases cover empty and one-item Lists. General Maybe values in other source positions and element families remain open.

The exact standard-library export is absent. Scoped direct support uses blockTimeBefore(UInt64 deadline), which compares Unix-second current time < deadline. Lean, Compact 0.36.1 and native checks cover the strict boundary and guarded case. The finalized receipt uses both strict kernel predicates, not this exact standard-library export. Full equivalence and hosted-context integration remain unverified.

No direct non-strict helper is evidenced. The related strict blockTimeBefore(UInt64 deadline) result can be inverted with select(result, false, true) to express current time >= deadline. Evidence covers the strict operand and Bool select, not a differential case or finalized call for this exact helper. Full equivalence remains unverified.

The exact standard-library export is absent. Scoped direct support uses blockTimeAfter(UInt64 deadline), which compares deadline < Unix-second current time. Lean, Compact 0.36.1 and native checks cover the strict boundary and guarded case. The finalized receipt uses both strict kernel predicates, not this exact standard-library export. Full equivalence and hosted-context integration remain unverified.

No direct non-strict helper is evidenced. The related strict blockTimeAfter(UInt64 deadline) result can be inverted with select(result, false, true) to express current time <= deadline. Evidence covers the strict operand and Bool select, not a differential case or finalized call for this exact helper. Full equivalence remains unverified.

Direct scalar and fixed-byte source encoding uses explicit length and zero right padding. Focused Bool, UInt, Bytes, Native, and Secp256k1Scalar bytes match Compact 0.36.1. Readable named codecs and scalar helpers share this codec across native and hosted paths. The nested payment frame matches the pinned reference, and the readable source emits identical ZKIR to the earlier helper form. Payload-carrying wire enums and full conformance remain open.

Direct scalar and fixed-byte source decoding uses type-sized prefixes. Native, Bool and UInt bounds are checked. Foreign scalar decoding reduces by the target modulus. Readable named codecs decode records, tuples, vectors, bytes and fieldless enums using a fixed frame. Readable fixed projections feed private approval predicates and explicitly disclosed output. The authenticated host and native checker agree on the nested payment case and reject malformed UInt, Bool and enum values. Payload-carrying wire enums and full conformance remain open.
